sara-support: Customer on a Dedicated account (acme-x) is seeing intermittent 429s even though their reserved pool rsc-42 should allow 100 qps headroom. Happening at steady ~30 qps. Can we triage?

miguel: Thanks — can you paste a sample request/response (headers) + request IDs and rough timeframe? Is auth succeeding every time?

sara-support: timeframe 2025-11-02 09:00-09:20 UTC. Sample reply from our edge:```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Sun, 02 Nov 2025 09:05:12 GMT
X-Request-Id: rq_01F8ZK2X1
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1698933912
Content-Type: application/json
{ \"error\": \"rate_limited\" }```Auth token valid, no auth failures in logs.

liam: Noted. This smells like per-node token-shard exhaustion rather than global pool depletion. Dedicated pools use a token-bucket sharded across serving nodes; if traffic spikes/fans out unevenly you can hit a hot shard even though pool total shows headroom.

infra-oncall: I pulled serving metrics for rsc-42 around 09:05. Token shards: [shard0=18/25, shard1=0/25, shard2=22/25, shard3=1/25] — shard1 and shard3 drained repeatedly. QPS distribution across nodes was uneven due to client-side connection reuse pattern.

miguel: Repro suggestion: do 50 concurrent short-lived connections vs 1 long-lived streaming connection — the short-lived fanout tends to hit many nodes and cause per-shard depletion. Try this curl loop to reproduce quickly:```bash
for i in {1..60}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}' & done; wait
```

anna-support: Customer asks for a mitigation that doesn't touch their app. Can we provide an immediate fix? They need SLA guarantee intact.

infra-oncall: Short-term mitigation options: 1) enable cross-shard borrowing for rsc-42 (helps hotspots borrow tokens from underutilized shards), 2) bump per-shard bucket size, 3) route a small % (canary) of traffic to the shared fallback pool until we stabilize. To enable borrowing now:```rdctl pools update rsc-42 --enable-cross-shard-borrow=true```This is a control-plane change and takes ~30s to propagate.

liam: Note: enabling borrowing mitigates 429s but may slightly change latency percentiles under extreme pressure. It does not change billing tier. If we bump per-shard quotas we consume more capacity for that pool (could affect other customers during peak) — so prefer borrowing + smoothing.

miguel: Timeline from graphs: 09:00 15 qps, 09:04 burst to 48 qps (60s), 09:06 fanout spike to 90 qps across nodes (sustained 20s), 09:07 back to 30 qps. 429s clustered at 09:04-09:07.

anna-support: I'll draft customer message. Suggest: "We identified per-node rate shard hotspots causing transient 429s during short fanout bursts. We're enabling temporary cross-shard borrowing for your reserved pool and recommending a client-side smoothing change. This will prevent further 429s while we monitor." Want to include an ETA.

infra-oncall: Action items: 1) enable cross-shard borrowing for rsc-42 (now) 2) add short-term routing to shared fallback if errors persist 3) post-mortem: evaluate pool shard_count vs active serving nodes and enable adaptive shard rebalancer (JIRA INF-5423). I'll run the rdctl command and comment here.

rd-bot: rdctl: executed pools update rsc-42 --enable-cross-shard-borrow=true — success (applied by infra-oncall). Propagation started at 2468101279.

liam: After change we saw shard utilization smooth out within a minute, no further 429s in the 09:10-09:20 window. Recommend long-term: set shard_count = max(ceil(nodes * 0.75), 4) and enable adaptive rebalancer.

sara-support: Thanks all — I'll send the customer the drafted message and keep monitoring. cc @anna-support for copy. :thumbsup:

anna-support: Draft sent at 09:22 UTC, customer acknowledged and asked for a follow-up runbook. Creating support playbook: SP-ACME-2025-11.

infra-oncall: Closing the triage thread. Follow-ups: INF-5423 (rebalancer), PL-MON-227 (shard metrics alert tuning).
